targets._doc: Targets for the text battle simulator (many battles on the real energy v2 rules). Rarer is allowed to win; peers must stay close; Ash should feel stronger with every level, evolution and slot.

rarity_step_winrate.doc: a species one rarity step up, at the same level and stage, wins this share against the step below (a clear, not absurd, step)

within_tier_winrate.doc: within one rarity at a similar level, no common or uncommon's average win rate against its peers leaves this band

targets.within_tier_spread_doc: the spread of the peers' average win rates in a tier, stat group and level band: the 10th to the 90th percentile (the full range is reported too)

starter_triangle.doc: each starter against the one it is strong against, at the same level and stage

evolution_step_winrate.doc: an evolved form against its previous stage at the evolution level

level_step_winrate.doc: a species against itself ten levels lower: a clear step up (new moves, a slot, more HP), not quite a wall

slot_unlock_winrate.doc: the same species with one more equip slot (the 'Ash gets stronger' lever)

targets.doc_first_mover: the side that acts first should not win much more than half
targets.doc_move_pick: no single move should be more than this share of a species' picks across battles (choice stays real)

dodge_success.doc: a Dodge against an attack that doesn't ignore it

battle_turns.doc: a typical battle's length in turns (the mean)

targets.doc_role_share: every role (offense, reaction, two-phase, disruption, utility) is at least this share of all actions; role_share sets a role's own min or max
targets.doc_tier_share: every tier (opener, mid, finisher) is at least this share of all actions; tier_share sets a tier's own min
targets.doc_exempt: weak by design (the joke fish and the cocoons, whose whole point is to evolve): left out of the peer band and spread checks; a design decision for the user

engine and AI fixes from the battle logs (by hand)
tuning_log.why: the planner now reads the battle's state (PkmnAI.state_ctx): a condition the foe already has is worth nothing and a stat change half per stage already moved, a status move twice in one plan is next to worthless (ai.status_repeat_turn), and the per-action bonus only counts for an action worth something; Thunder Wave on a paralysed foe now says so; paralysis is rolled once a turn (damage.para_scope turn). Pikachu Lv 9 had spent five turns on Thunder Wave and Tail Whip

a Kanto species' newest moves were often all status or off-pool (Pikachu Lv 9 equipped Thunder Wave, Charge, Dodge, Tail Whip and an off-pool Double Kick: no attack it could pay for). A wild or fresh one now equips an opener, a mid and a finisher it can pay, then a reaction, a disruption and a support move

in TCG mode only the card's weakness and resistance counted, so Fire hit Water at full power; the chart's 'not very effective' now takes a fifth off, so Water beats Fire both ways. A design call: the card game itself has no such rule

the planner spent spare chips on anything worth more than nothing (a second and third Tail Whip in one turn) because an unspent chip counts as waste; an action worth less than this now scores as no better than leaving the chips

tuning_log.change: the planner skips moves whose own rule would fail (by hand, engine)
tuning_log.why: Snorlax opened with Snore while awake ('But it failed!') and Last Resort hit for 94 before any other move was used; Last Resort now needs the others used first (the engine enforces it) and the planner leaves out Snore, Dream Eater, Raging Smash, Last Resort and Fake Out when they can't work
